**Ronald Antonio O'Sullivan** (born 5 December 1975) is an English professional [snooker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snooker "Snooker") player from [Chigwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chigwell "Chigwell"), [Essex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Essex "Essex"). He has won the [World Snooker Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Snooker_Championship "World Snooker Championship") seven times, a [modern-era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cue_sports_terms#modern_era "Glossary of cue sports terms") record he shares with [Stephen Hendry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Hendry "Stephen Hendry"). He has also won a record eight [Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masters_\(snooker\) "Masters \(snooker\)") and a record eight [UK Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Championship "UK Championship") titles, giving him 23 [Triple Crown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_Crown_\(snooker\) "Triple Crown \(snooker\)") titles, more than any other player. He holds the record for the most [ranking titles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_snooker_players_by_number_of_ranking_titles "List of snooker players by number of ranking titles"), with 41, and has been ranked [world number one](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_number_one_snooker_players "List of world number one snooker players") on five occasions.
After winning amateur titles including the [IBSF World Under-21 Snooker Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBSF_World_Under-21_Snooker_Championship "IBSF World Under-21 Snooker Championship"), O'Sullivan turned professional in 1992, aged 16. He did so alongside [John Higgins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Higgins "John Higgins") and [Mark Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Williams_\(snooker_player\) "Mark Williams \(snooker player\)"), and the three players are known collectively as the "[Class of '92](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_of_'92_\(snooker\) "Class of '92 \(snooker\)")". He won the [1993 UK Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_UK_Championship "1993 UK Championship") at age 17 to become the youngest ranking-event winner, a record that still stands. He is also the youngest winner of the Masters and the oldest winner of all three Triple Crown events. He has featured at the [Crucible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crucible_Theatre "Crucible Theatre") more times than any other player, with 34 appearances as of the [2026 event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_World_Snooker_Championship "2026 World Snooker Championship").
O'Sullivan made his first competitive [century break](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Century_break "Century break") at age 10 and his first competitive [maximum break](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_break "Maximum break") at age 15. He was the first player to make 1,000 centuries in professional competition, and has since passed 1,300 centuries. He holds the record for the most officially recognised maximums in professional competition, with 17, and holds the [Guinness World Record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness_World_Records "Guinness World Records") for the fastest competitive maximum, made in 5 minutes and 8 seconds at the [1997 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_World_Snooker_Championship "1997 World Snooker Championship"). At the [2026 World Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_World_Open_\(snooker\) "2026 World Open \(snooker\)"), he made a [16-red clearance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cue_sports_terms#16-red_clearance "Glossary of cue sports terms") of 153, the highest break in professional snooker history.
O'Sullivan has experienced depression, mood swings, and drug and alcohol abuse during his career. An outspoken and controversial figure on the [professional tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Snooker_Tour "World Snooker Tour"), he has been disciplined several times by the [World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Professional_Billiards_and_Snooker_Association "World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association") for his behaviour and comments. Away from the table, he has worked as a television [pundit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pundit "Pundit") and has written crime novels, autobiographies, and a health and fitness book. He is the subject of the 2023 documentary film _[Ronnie O'Sullivan: The Edge of Everything](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan:_The_Edge_of_Everything "Ronnie O'Sullivan: The Edge of Everything")._ He was inducted into the [World Snooker Tour Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Snooker_Tour_awards "World Snooker Tour awards") in 2012 and was appointed [OBE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Most_Excellent_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Officer of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire") in the [2016 New Year Honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_New_Year_Honours "2016 New Year Honours"). In 2025, he relocated to Dubai.
## Career summary
Main article: [Professional snooker career of Ronnie O'Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_snooker_career_of_Ronnie_O'Sullivan "Professional snooker career of Ronnie O'Sullivan")
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Ronnie_O%E2%80%99Sullivan_at_German_Masters_Snooker_Final_%28DerHexer%29_2012-02-05_65.jpg/250px-Ronnie_O%E2%80%99Sullivan_at_German_Masters_Snooker_Final_%28DerHexer%29_2012-02-05_65.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ronnie_O%E2%80%99Sullivan_at_German_Masters_Snooker_Final_\(DerHexer\)_2012-02-05_65.jpg)O'Sullivan with the [2012 German Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_German_Masters "2012 German Masters") trophy
O'Sullivan began playing snooker at age 7 and soon became a noted amateur competitor, winning his first [club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billiard_room "Billiard room") tournament at age 9, making his first competitive [century break](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Century_break "Century break") at age 10,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-2) and winning the [British Under-16 Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Junior_Snooker_Championship "British Junior Snooker Championship") at age 13.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-u16-3) At the 1991 [English Amateur Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Amateur_Championship "English Amateur Championship"), aged 15 years and 98 days, he made his first competitive [maximum break](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_break "Maximum break"), then the youngest player ever to do so in a recognised tournament.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-Ronnie_Record_Breaker-4) In the same year, he won the [IBSF World Under-21 Snooker Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBSF_World_Under-21_Snooker_Championship "IBSF World Under-21 Snooker Championship") and [Junior Pot Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_Junior_Pot_Black "1991 Junior Pot Black").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-6)
After turning professional in 1992, aged 16, he won 74 of his first 76 qualifying matches,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-History_of_Snooker-7) including a record 38 consecutive professional victories.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-Ronnie_Record_Breaker-4) He qualified for the televised stages of the [1993 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_World_Snooker_Championship "1993 World Snooker Championship"), losing 10–7 to [Alan McManus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_McManus "Alan McManus") on his Crucible debut. He claimed his first ranking title later that year, beating Hendry 10–6 in the final of the [1993 UK Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_UK_Championship "1993 UK Championship") seven days before his 18th birthday to become the youngest-ever winner of a ranking event, a record he still holds.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-SLife2020-8) In the [following season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994%E2%80%9395_snooker_season "1994–95 snooker season"), he won the [1995 Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_Masters_\(snooker\) "1995 Masters \(snooker\)") aged 19 years and 69 days to become the youngest Masters champion.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-9)
Between 1996 and 1999, O'Sullivan reached three World semi-finals in four years. At the [1997 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_World_Snooker_Championship "1997 World Snooker Championship"), he achieved his first [maximum break](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_break "Maximum break") in professional competition. Compiled in a time of 5 minutes and 8 seconds, it remains the [fastest competitive maximum break](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_break#fastest "Maximum break") in snooker history, which is listed as a Guinness World Record.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-Deadspin-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-11) He won his second UK title later that year at the [1997 UK Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_UK_Championship "1997 UK Championship").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-BBC02Profile-12) Despite these successes, his career also became marred by controversy in the late 1990s. During the [1996 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_World_Snooker_Championship "1996 World Snooker Championship"), he assaulted an assistant press officer, for which he received a suspended two-year ban and a £20,000 fine.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-Independent07012010-13) After winning the [1998 Irish Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_Irish_Masters "1998 Irish Masters"), he was stripped of his title and prize money when a post-match drug test found evidence of cannabis in his system.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-14) O'Sullivan subsequently acknowledged frequent abuse of drugs and alcohol in the early years of his career, which resulted in spells in the [Priory Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priory_Hospital "Priory Hospital") for rehabilitation.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-15)
He reached his first World final in [2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_World_Snooker_Championship "2001 World Snooker Championship"), where he defeated [John Higgins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Higgins "John Higgins") 18–14 to claim his first World title and reached number two in the world rankings.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-BBC02Profile-12) He won his third [UK Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_UK_Championship "2001 UK Championship") later that year,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-WPBSABio-16) which helped him attain the [world number one](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_number_one_snooker_players "List of world number one snooker players") ranking for the first time in the [2002–03 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snooker_world_rankings_2002/2003 "Snooker world rankings 2002/2003"). With veteran six-time World Champion [Ray Reardon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Reardon "Ray Reardon") acting as his coach and mentor, he won his second World title in [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_World_Snooker_Championship "2004 World Snooker Championship"), defeating [Graeme Dott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graeme_Dott "Graeme Dott") 18–8 in the final,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-17) after which he held the number one ranking for the next two seasons. He added his second Masters title in [2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Masters_\(snooker\) "2005 Masters \(snooker\)"), ten years after his first.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-18) His behaviour became notably erratic in the mid-2000s as he battled [clinical depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_depressive_disorder "Major depressive disorder"). During the [2005 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Snooker_Championship "2005 World Snooker Championship"), he shaved his head mid-tournament and exhibited what _[The Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Independent "The Independent")_ called a "public emotional disintegration" while losing 11 of the last 14 frames in his quarter-final defeat against [Peter Ebdon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Ebdon "Peter Ebdon").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-19) At the [2005 UK Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UK_Championship "2005 UK Championship"), he sat with a wet towel draped over his head during his match against [Mark King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_King_\(snooker_player\) "Mark King \(snooker player\)").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-TimesOSullivan-20) Trailing Hendry 4–1 in their best-of-17-frames quarter-final at the [2006 UK Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_UK_Championship "2006 UK Championship"), he abruptly conceded the match during the sixth frame and left the arena. Hendry was awarded the match 9–1 and O'Sullivan was fined £20,800 over the incident.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-Independent07012010-13)
In 2007, O'Sullivan won his third [Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Masters_\(snooker\) "2007 Masters \(snooker\)") title and his fourth [UK Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_UK_Championship "2007 UK Championship"), which was his first ranking title in almost three years.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-WPBSABio-16) He won his third World title in [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_World_Snooker_Championship "2008 World Snooker Championship"), defeating [Ali Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Carter "Ali Carter") 18–8 in the final,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-21) after which he held the world number one ranking for the next two seasons. He added his fourth Masters title in [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Masters_\(snooker\) "2009 Masters \(snooker\)").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-WPBSABio-16) After two poor seasons that saw him fall out of the top ten in the world rankings for the first time, he began working with psychiatrist [Steve Peters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Peters_\(psychiatrist\) "Steve Peters \(psychiatrist\)") in 2011.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-ESPN2013-22) A resurgent O'Sullivan captured his fourth World title in [2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_World_Snooker_Championship "2012 World Snooker Championship"), defeating Carter 18–11 in the final, after which he paid tribute to Peters' work with him.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-23) In the [following season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_snooker_season "2012–13 snooker season"), he took an extended break from the professional tour.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-ESPN2013-22) Despite having played only one competitive match all season, he returned to the Crucible for the [2013 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Snooker_Championship "2013 World Snooker Championship") and successfully defended his World title, defeating [Barry Hawkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Hawkins "Barry Hawkins") 18–12 in the final.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-24) In his [2014 Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Masters_\(snooker\) "2014 Masters \(snooker\)") quarter-final against [Ricky Walden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Walden "Ricky Walden"), he set a new record for the most points scored without reply in professional competition, with 556,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-25) and went on to beat the defending champion [Mark Selby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Selby "Mark Selby") 10–4 in the final to claim his fifth Masters title.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-26) At the [2014 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Snooker_Championship "2014 World Snooker Championship"), he reached a third consecutive world final, where he again faced Selby. Despite taking a 10–5 lead, O'Sullivan lost 18–14, his first defeat in a world final.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-27) Later in 2014, he won his fifth [UK Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_UK_Championship "2014 UK Championship"), beating [Judd Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judd_Trump "Judd Trump") 10–9 in the final. However, he declined to defend his title the following year and pulled out of the [2015 UK Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UK_Championship "2015 UK Championship"), citing debilitating insomnia.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-28) At the [2015 Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Masters_\(snooker\) "2015 Masters \(snooker\)"), he made his 776th century break in professional competition, surpassing Hendry's record for the most career centuries.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-29)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Ronnie_O%27Sullivan_with_World_Championship_Trophy_2013.jpg/250px-Ronnie_O%27Sullivan_with_World_Championship_Trophy_2013.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ronnie_O'Sullivan_with_World_Championship_Trophy_2013.jpg)O'Sullivan after winning his fifth World title in [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Snooker_Championship "2013 World Snooker Championship")
O'Sullivan won two consecutive Masters tournaments in [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Masters_\(snooker\) "2016 Masters \(snooker\)") and [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Masters_\(snooker\) "2017 Masters \(snooker\)") for a record seven Masters titles. He also won two consecutive UK Championships in [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_UK_Championship "2017 UK Championship") and [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_UK_Championship "2018 UK Championship") for a record seven UK titles, attaining a total of 19 Triple Crown titles to surpass Hendry's total of 18. During the [2017–18 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_snooker_season "2017–18 snooker season"), he won five ranking events.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-30) He defeated [Neil Robertson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Robertson "Neil Robertson") 10–4 in the final to win the [2019 Players Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Players_Championship_\(snooker\) "2019 Players Championship \(snooker\)"). In the last frame of the match, he made his 1,000th century break in professional competition, becoming the first player to reach that milestone.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-31) He won his 36th ranking title at the [2019 Tour Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Tour_Championship "2019 Tour Championship"), equalling Hendry's record and attaining the world number one ranking for the first time since May 2010.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-32)
At the [2020 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_World_Snooker_Championship "2020 World Snooker Championship"), O'Sullivan came from 14 to 16 behind in the semi-final against Selby to win 17–16. He then defeated [Kyren Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyren_Wilson "Kyren Wilson") 18–8 in the final to win his sixth world title. The tournament marked his 28th consecutive Crucible appearance, surpassing Hendry's record of 27 consecutive appearances.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-SLife2020-8) He reached his 58th ranking final at the [2021 Tour Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Tour_Championship "2021 Tour Championship"), breaking Hendry's record of 57 ranking final appearances,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-33) but lost 10–4 to [Neil Robertson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Robertson "Neil Robertson"). During the tournament, he made his 1,100th century break in professional competition.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-34) He lost five consecutive ranking finals in the [2020–21 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020%E2%80%9321_snooker_season "2020–21 snooker season"), but ended a 16-month title drought by winning his 38th ranking title at the [2021 World Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_World_Grand_Prix_\(snooker\) "2021 World Grand Prix \(snooker\)").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-35)
O'Sullivan defeated Trump 18–13 in the [2022 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Snooker_Championship "2022 World Snooker Championship") final to win his seventh world title, equalling Hendry for the most world titles in the [modern era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Snooker_Championship#Start_of_modern_era_knockout_tournaments_\(1969%E2%80%931976\) "World Snooker Championship").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-SeventhWorldTitle-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-37) Aged 46 years and 148 days, he became the oldest World Champion in snooker history, surpassing Reardon, who won his last title in [1978](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_World_Snooker_Championship "1978 World Snooker Championship") aged 45 years and 203 days.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-38) O'Sullivan also surpassed Hendry's record of 70 Crucible wins, setting a new record of 74.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-39)
O'Sullivan defeated [Marco Fu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Fu "Marco Fu") 6–4 to win the [2022 Hong Kong Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Hong_Kong_Masters "2022 Hong Kong Masters"). The final was played before an estimated 9,000 spectators, the largest audience ever to attend a snooker match.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-40) At the [2023 World Snooker Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Snooker_Championship "2023 World Snooker Championship"), O'Sullivan made a record 31st Crucible appearance, surpassing the previous record of 30 by [Steve Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Davis "Steve Davis").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-41) He made his 200th Crucible century break and his 1,200th century in professional competition during his second-round match against [Hossein Vafaei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hossein_Vafaei "Hossein Vafaei").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-42) His reached the quarter-final, becoming the first player to compete in 100 matches at the Crucible,[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-43) but lost 10–13 to eventual winner [Luca Brecel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luca_Brecel "Luca Brecel").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-44)
At the invitational [2023 Shanghai Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Shanghai_Masters "2023 Shanghai Masters"), O'Sullivan defeated Brecel 11–9 in the final to claim his fourth consecutive, and fifth total, [Shanghai Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Masters_\(snooker\) "Shanghai Masters \(snooker\)") title, extending his winning streak at the tournament to 18 matches since [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Shanghai_Masters "2017 Shanghai Masters").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-45) He won record-extending eighth titles at both the [2023 UK Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_UK_Championship "2023 UK Championship") and the [2024 Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Masters_\(snooker\) "2024 Masters \(snooker\)"), respectively defeating [Ding Junhui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ding_Junhui "Ding Junhui") and Ali Carter 10–7 in the finals. This extended his record number of ranking titles to 40 and Triple Crown titles to 23. Aged 47 years and 363 days when he won the UK Championship, and 48 years and 40 days when he won the Masters, he became the oldest winner of all three Triple Crown events.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-46) He also became simultaneously the youngest and oldest winner of both the UK Championship and the Masters.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-48) He won his 41st ranking title at the [2024 World Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_World_Grand_Prix_\(snooker\) "2024 World Grand Prix \(snooker\)") with a 10–7 victory over Trump in the final,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-49) and went on to win the invitational [2024 World Masters of Snooker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_World_Masters_of_Snooker "2024 World Masters of Snooker"), the first professional snooker tournament held in Saudi Arabia, defeating Brecel 5–2 in the final.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-50) He signed a three-year ambassadorial deal with Saudi Arabia, which requires him to play in all World Snooker Tour events staged in that country, to establish a snooker academy in the Middle East, and to contribute to the development of the sport in the region.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-51) At the [2024 Shanghai Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Shanghai_Masters "2024 Shanghai Masters"), O'Sullivan lost 3–10 to Trump in the semi-finals, his first defeat at the tournament since 2016, after 20 consecutive match wins.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-52)
During the [2024–25 snooker season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_snooker_season "2024–25 snooker season"), O'Sullivan withdrew from nine tournaments, including the [2025 Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Masters_\(snooker\) "2025 Masters \(snooker\)"), the [2025 German Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_German_Masters "2025 German Masters"), the [2025 Welsh Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Welsh_Open_\(snooker\) "2025 Welsh Open \(snooker\)"), and the [2025 World Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Grand_Prix_\(snooker\) "2025 World Grand Prix \(snooker\)").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-53) He returned to competition at the 2025 World Championship after a three-month break.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-54) At the [2025 Saudi Arabia Snooker Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Saudi_Arabia_Snooker_Masters "2025 Saudi Arabia Snooker Masters"), he made his 16th and 17th official maximum breaks in his semi-final match against [Chris Wakelin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Wakelin "Chris Wakelin"). He became the second player, after [Jackson Page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Page "Jackson Page"), to make two maximums in the same match, and the first to do so in a one-session match or on the same day. At the age of 49 years and 253 days, he became the oldest player to record an official maximum. He won a £147,000 bonus for making the two breaks in one of the four major tournaments of the season.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-56) In his quarter-final match against [Ryan Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Day_\(snooker_player\) "Ryan Day \(snooker player\)") at the [2026 World Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_World_Open_\(snooker\) "2026 World Open \(snooker\)"), O'Sullivan made the highest break in professional snooker history, a [16-red clearance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cue_sports_terms#16-red_clearance "Glossary of cue sports terms") of 153. It was only the second time that a [break exceeding 147](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_break#Breaks_exceeding_147 "Maximum break") had been made in professional competition, following a 148 by [Jamie Burnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Burnett "Jamie Burnett") in 2004.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-57)
O'Sullivan's other career highlights include three [World Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Grand_Prix_\(snooker\) "World Grand Prix \(snooker\)") titles, two [Players Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Players_Championship_\(snooker\) "Players Championship \(snooker\)") titles, four [Welsh Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welsh_Open_\(snooker\) "Welsh Open \(snooker\)") titles, two [Scottish Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Open_\(snooker\) "Scottish Open \(snooker\)") titles, two [German Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Masters "German Masters") titles, four [Irish Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Masters "Irish Masters") titles, two [China Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Open_\(snooker\) "China Open \(snooker\)") titles, two [Champions Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_Cup_\(snooker\) "Champions Cup \(snooker\)") titles, ten [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League_Snooker "Premier League Snooker") titles, four [Champion of Champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champion_of_Champions_\(snooker\) "Champion of Champions \(snooker\)") titles, three [Scottish Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Masters "Scottish Masters") titles, and five [Shanghai Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Masters_\(snooker\) "Shanghai Masters \(snooker\)") titles.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-WPBSABio-16)
## Playing style
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/eb/Ronnie_O%27Sullivan_PHC_2011-1.png/250px-Ronnie_O%27Sullivan_PHC_2011-1.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ronnie_O'Sullivan_PHC_2011-1.png)O'Sullivan during the [2011 Paul Hunter Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Paul_Hunter_Classic "2011 Paul Hunter Classic")
Known for his fast and attacking style of play, O'Sullivan gained the nickname "The Rocket" after winning a best-of-nine frame match in a record 43 minutes during his [debut season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992%E2%80%9393_snooker_season "1992–93 snooker season") as a professional.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-58) A prolific break builder and great tactical player, he has stated his disdain for long, drawn-out games, saying that they harm the game of snooker.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-59) O'Sullivan is [ambidextrous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambidexterity "Ambidexterity"), as he is right-handed but can play to a high standard with his left hand and routinely alternates when needed, enabling him to attempt shots with his left hand that would otherwise require a [rest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cue_sports_terms#cross "Glossary of cue sports terms") or [spider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cue_sports_terms#spider "Glossary of cue sports terms").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-troubled_genius-60) When he first displayed this left-handed ability in the [1996 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_World_Snooker_Championship "1996 World Snooker Championship") against [Alain Robidoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Robidoux "Alain Robidoux"), the Canadian accused him of disrespect and refused to shake hands after the match.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-Independent07012010-13)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-61)
## Status
O'Sullivan is highly regarded in snooker, with several of his peers regarding him as the greatest player ever,[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-Reardon-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-66) and some labelling him a "genius".[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-no_ordinary-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-68) After losing 17–6 to O'Sullivan in the [2008 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_World_Snooker_Championship "2008 World Snooker Championship") semi-final, Hendry described him as "the best player in the world by a country mile".[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-69) In 2024, Hendry agreed that there was no longer any question as to whether O'Sullivan was the greatest snooker player of all time, also calling him an "artist".[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-70) However, O'Sullivan has dismissed the suggestion that he is the greatest player and has identified Hendry as the greatest due to his domination of snooker.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-71)
One of the most popular players on the circuit,[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-72) he is noted for being a "showman",[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-73) and is credited with helping improve the image of snooker with the general public.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-no_ordinary-67)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-74) He has often been compared with [Alex Higgins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Higgins "Alex Higgins") and [Jimmy White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_White "Jimmy White") for his natural talent and popularity.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-troubled_genius-60) In [December 2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_BBC_Sports_Personality_of_the_Year_Award "2020 BBC Sports Personality of the Year Award"), O'Sullivan was nominated for the BBC's [Sports Personality of the Year Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Sports_Personality_of_the_Year_Award "BBC Sports Personality of the Year Award"), becoming the first snooker player to receive a nomination since Hendry in 1990.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-75)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-:0-76) He was nominated for a second time in [December 2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_BBC_Sports_Personality_of_the_Year_Award "2022 BBC Sports Personality of the Year Award").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-:0-76)
O'Sullivan sometimes lacks confidence or interest,[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-Dec06-77) and has performed inconsistently throughout his career,[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-78) with observers noting the "two Ronnies" aspect of his character.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-79)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-80)
He has received praise from athletes in other sports. Tennis player [Novak Djokovic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novak_Djokovic "Novak Djokovic") called him "one of the sport greats".[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-81)
## Criticisms of snooker
After [Barry Hearn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Hearn "Barry Hearn") took charge of [World Snooker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Snooker_Tour "World Snooker Tour") in 2010, O'Sullivan became a vocal critic of how Hearn reconfigured the professional tour. He took issue with increased travel expectations, flat 128 draws that required top professionals to play more rounds against lower-ranked opponents, reduced prize money for maximum breaks, and tournament venues he saw as inadequate. He accused snooker's governing body [WPBSA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Professional_Billiards_and_Snooker_Association "World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association") of bullying and intimidating him, said that Hearn was running a "dictatorship",[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-82) protested alleged mistreatment by snooker's authorities by giving robotic or monosyllabic responses in interviews,[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-83) and refused opportunities to make maximum breaks in apparent protest over inadequate prize money for the achievement.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-84) In 2018, he threatened to form a breakaway snooker tour akin to the [split in darts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Split_in_darts "Split in darts").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-85)
During the [2020 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_World_Snooker_Championship "2020 World Snooker Championship"), O'Sullivan publicly criticised the standard of new players coming into snooker, stating that he would have to "lose an arm and a leg to fall out of the top 50".[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-86) He was also critical of the tournament organisers' decision to allow fans into the final during the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-87)
In 2021, O'Sullivan claimed on a podcast interview that most snooker players had wasted their lives. He called snooker a "bad sport" that can cause "a lot of damage", suggesting that the [antisocial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asociality "Asociality") nature of solitary practice in a darkened environment can stunt players' personal development. He stated that he would not support his own children if they chose to become snooker players, and said that if he could live his sporting career over again, he would pursue [golf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golf "Golf") or [Formula One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One") instead.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-88)
## Other endeavours
### Broadcasting
[Eurosport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurosport "Eurosport") signed an exclusive deal with O'Sullivan in March 2014 to make him its global ambassador for snooker, with the goal of driving its international appeal.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-89) As part of this deal, O'Sullivan created a special snooker series for the network called _The Ronnie O'Sullivan Show_ , which included his insights into the game, interviews with other professional players, and playing tips. He also wrote for [Yahoo!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahoo! "Yahoo!") websites and [mobile apps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_application_software "Mobile application software") during the [2014 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Snooker_Championship "2014 World Snooker Championship").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-90) He frequently appears as a [pundit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pundit "Pundit") on Eurosport's snooker coverage, alongside Jimmy White and [Neal Foulds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neal_Foulds "Neal Foulds").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
In 2015 and 2016, O'Sullivan co-hosted the _Midweek Matchzone_ show with Chris Hood on [Brentwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brentwood,_Essex "Brentwood, Essex") radio station [Phoenix FM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_FM "Phoenix FM").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-91) In 2017, he starred in miniseries _Ronnie O'Sullivan's American Hustle_ with broadcasting friend [Matt Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Smith_\(broadcaster\) "Matt Smith \(broadcaster\)"), in which the pair toured different cities in the United States learning the art of [pool hustling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pool_hustling "Pool hustling").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-92)
### Author
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Ronnie_O%E2%80%99Sullivan_at_Snooker_German_Masters_%28Martin_Rulsch%29_2014-01-30_07.jpg/250px-Ronnie_O%E2%80%99Sullivan_at_Snooker_German_Masters_%28Martin_Rulsch%29_2014-01-30_07.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ronnie_O%E2%80%99Sullivan_at_Snooker_German_Masters_\(Martin_Rulsch\)_2014-01-30_07.jpg)O'Sullivan at a 2014 book signing
O'Sullivan has written three crime novels in collaboration with author Emlyn Rees:[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-93) _Framed_ (2016),[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-BBC20160707-94) _Double Kiss_ (2017),[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-95) and _The Break_ (2018). Although the novels are not autobiographical, they are loosely based on his early experiences and family life.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-BBC20160707-94) He has also written two autobiographies. His first, _Ronnie: The Autobiography of Ronnie O'Sullivan_ , was published in 2003; and his second, _Running: The Autobiography_ , was published in 2013.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-96) He has also co-authored a health and fitness book with nutritionist [Rhiannon Lambert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhiannon_Lambert "Rhiannon Lambert") entitled _Top of Your Game: Eating for Mind and Body_. Published in 2019, it contains healthy recipes and advice for "living better, eating healthier and feeding your brain to enhance your performance".[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-97)
### Video games
O'Sullivan has been involved with several video games, including _[Virtual Snooker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_Snooker "Virtual Snooker")_ (1996), _[World Snooker Championship 2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Snooker_Championship_2007_\(video_game\) "World Snooker Championship 2007 \(video game\)")_ (2007), and _Ronnie O'Sullivan's Snooker_ for [PlayStation Portable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable "PlayStation Portable") (2012).[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-98)
### Documentary film
Main article: [Ronnie O'Sullivan: The Edge of Everything](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan:_The_Edge_of_Everything "Ronnie O'Sullivan: The Edge of Everything")
A documentary film titled _[Ronnie O'Sullivan: The Edge of Everything](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan:_The_Edge_of_Everything "Ronnie O'Sullivan: The Edge of Everything")_ was produced by [David Beckham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Beckham "David Beckham")'s production company Studio 99, directed by filmmaker Sam Blair, and distributed by MetFilms.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-99) The film premiered in London on 21 November 2023, and was released on [Amazon Prime Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Prime_Video "Amazon Prime Video") on 23 November. It highlighted the hardships he faced as a professional at the highest level of snooker, as well as how his personal life had impacted his career.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-100)
### Snooker course
In October 2023, O'Sullivan launched an online snooker course entitled The Rocket Method, where he provides in-depth lessons on the game for a subscription fee.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-101) Assisted by Alan McManus, the course contains 12 episodes, each an hour in length, of which the final batch of episodes was released in March 2024.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-snooker.online-102) The course has a cinematic production and was directed by [Oscar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")-nominated director Gregg Helvey, and episodes are available in English and Mandarin Chinese.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-snooker.online-102)
## Personal life
O'Sullivan was born on 5 December 1975 in [Wordsley, West Midlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wordsley "Wordsley"),[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-WorldSnooker_Bio_of_O'Sullivan-103)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-Dec06-77)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-History_Bio_of_O'Sullivan-104) the son of Ronald John and Maria ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N%C3%A9e "Née") Catalano) O'Sullivan, who ran a string of [sex shops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_shop "Sex shop") in the [Soho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soho "Soho") area of London.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-Financial_Times_Oct_2013-105) His mother is originally from [Sicily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sicily "Sicily"), and O'Sullivan spent childhood holidays in the village near [Agrigento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agrigento "Agrigento") where she grew up.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-106) He was brought up in the Manor Road area of [Chigwell, Essex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chigwell "Chigwell"), where he lived for some years[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-Financial_Times_Oct_2013-105)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-107) and attended [Wanstead High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wanstead_High_School "Wanstead High School").[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-108) As of mid-2024, he lived in the adjoining area of [Chingford and Woodford Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chingford_and_Woodford_Green_\(UK_Parliament_constituency\) "Chingford and Woodford Green \(UK Parliament constituency\)").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-109)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-110) He is a first cousin of snooker player [Maria Catalano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Catalano "Maria Catalano"), who has been ranked number one in the women's game.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-111) In 1992 his father was sentenced to life in prison for [murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_in_English_law "Murder O'Sullivan has three children: a daughter from a two-year relationship with Sally Magnus,[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-115) as well as a son and a daughter from a relationship with Jo Langley, whom he met at [Narcotics Anonymous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narcotics_Anonymous "Narcotics Anonymous").[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-PC-116)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-117) He became a grandfather in October 2018 after his daughter with Sally Magnus gave birth to a daughter.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-118) He began dating actress [Laila Rouass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laila_Rouass "Laila Rouass") in 2012, and became engaged to her in 2013.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-119) Rouass announced on social media in February 2022 that they had ended their ten-year relationship.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-120) The couple later reconciled,[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-121) but in September 2024 were reported to have broken up again.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-122) They reconciled again in January 2025 and, in June of that year, they married at St George's Town Hall in [Shadwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shadwell "Shadwell"), East London.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-123)
O'Sullivan is known for his perfectionism and for being highly self-critical,[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-124)[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-125) even in victory.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-WC2008-126)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-127) Early in his career, he was treated for drug-related issues and bouts of depression.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-128) Since 2011, psychiatrist and sports psychologist [Steve Peters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Peters_\(psychiatrist\) "Steve Peters \(psychiatrist\)"), a close friend,[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-129)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-130) has helped him overcome his [mood swings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mood_swing "Mood swing").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-Financial_Times_Oct_2013-105)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-131) He is also a close friend of artist [Damien Hirst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damien_Hirst "Damien Hirst").[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-132) Noted for repeatedly declaring his intention to retire,[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-Telegraph_2012_May_4-133) O'Sullivan took an extended break from the professional snooker tour during the [2012–13 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_snooker_season "2012–13 snooker season"), during which he worked on a pig farm for several weeks.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-134) He enjoys running,[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-135) and has achieved a personal best of 34 minutes and 54 seconds for [10 km races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10K_run "10K run"), which ranked him in the top 1,500 10 km runners in the UK in 2008.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-136) O'Sullivan has _[plantar fasciitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plantar_fasciitis "Plantar fasciitis")_ , which led to him being granted an exemption from wearing the otherwise mandatory black leather shoes when playing snooker.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-137)
He enjoys cooking,[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-138) and appeared on the BBC's _[Saturday Kitchen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Kitchen "Saturday Kitchen")_ in December 2014 and February 2021.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-139) He also enjoys motor racing, and has appeared on series 4 of _[Top Gear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Gear_\(2002_TV_series\) "Top Gear \(2002 TV series\)")_.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-140)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-141) He is a supporter of [Arsenal F.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.")[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-142)
Despite a self-professed interest in [Islam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam "Islam"), O'Sullivan denied media reports that said he had converted to the religion in 2003.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-143)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-144)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-145)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-146) He has also espoused an interest in [Buddhism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhism "Buddhism"),[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-147) having spent many lunchtimes at the [London Buddhist Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Buddhist_Centre "London Buddhist Centre") in [Bethnal Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethnal_Green "Bethnal Green"). He has said he does not have a firm commitment to any religion.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-148)
O'Sullivan was made an [OBE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Most_Excellent_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Officer of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire") in the [New Year Honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Year_Honours "New Year Honours") list in 2016, for services to snooker.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-149)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-150)
O'Sullivan was a supporter of the [Labour Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labour_Party_\(UK\) "Labour Party \(UK\)") during the leadership of [Jeremy Corbyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Corbyn "Jeremy Corbyn"),[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-151)[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-152) but in June 2024, he endorsed [Faiza Shaheen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faiza_Shaheen "Faiza Shaheen"), the independent candidate for [Chingford and Woodford Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chingford_and_Woodford_Green_\(UK_Parliament_constituency\) "Chingford and Woodford Green \(UK Parliament constituency\)"), in the [2024 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_Kingdom_general_election "2024 United Kingdom general election").[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-153)[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-154)
In June 2023 he was a guest for BBC Radio 4's _[Desert Island Discs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desert_Island_Discs "Desert Island Discs")_. An extended version of the programme was broadcast in October 2024. His book choice was _Running with the Kenyans_ by [Adharanand Finn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adharanand_Finn "Adharanand Finn"), his luxury item was a painting set and his favourite disc was "[That's All](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That's_All_\(Genesis_song\) "That's All \(Genesis song\)")" by [Genesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genesis_\(band\) "Genesis \(band\)").[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-155)
On 31 October 2024, O'Sullivan obtained [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong") residency under the [Quality Migrant Admission Scheme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quality_Migrant_Admission_Scheme "Quality Migrant Admission Scheme").[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-156) In 2025, he moved to Dubai.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-157)

## Maximum and century breaks
Main article: [Maximum and century breaks made by Ronnie O'Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_and_century_breaks_made_by_Ronnie_O'Sullivan "Maximum and century breaks made by Ronnie O'Sullivan")
In March 2026 at the World Open, O’Sullivan achieved a break of 153, the highest ever in professional competition, potting 16 reds as a result of a free ball.[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-272)
O'Sullivan has completed 17 [maximum breaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_break "Maximum break") in professional competition, from his first in the [1997 World Snooker Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_World_Snooker_Championship "1997 World Snooker Championship") against [Mick Price](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Price_\(snooker_player\) "Mick Price \(snooker player\)")[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-O'Sullivan_1997_WC_Championship_max-273) to his second of two [2025 Saudi Arabia Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Saudi_Arabia_Masters "2025 Saudi Arabia Masters") maximums against [Chris Wakelin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Wakelin "Chris Wakelin").[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-274)
His first official maximum in 1997, completed in 5 minutes and 8 seconds, holds the record for the fastest maximum break achieved in competitive play. Initially, _[Guinness World Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness_World_Records "Guinness World Records")_ recorded the time at 5 minutes and 20 seconds,[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-275) but subsequent evidence has suggested that the BBC started the timer too early on the break.[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-276) Depending on the timing methodology used, the break took between 5 minutes 8 seconds and 5 minutes 15 seconds;[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-Deadspin-10) both [World Snooker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Snooker "World Snooker") and _Guinness World Records_ now officially acknowledge the shorter time.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-WorldSnooker_Bio_of_O'Sullivan-103)[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-277)
O'Sullivan also holds the record for the total number of [century breaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Century_break "Century break"), compiling more than 1,300 in professional competition. At the [2022 Scottish Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Scottish_Open_\(snooker\) "2022 Scottish Open \(snooker\)"), O'Sullivan scored a century in 3 minutes and 34 seconds—just 3 seconds slower than the fastest televised century break, made by [Tony Drago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Drago "Tony Drago") in 1996.[[261]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-278) He scored his 1,300th century in the [2025 Saudi Arabia Snooker Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Saudi_Arabia_Snooker_Masters "2025 Saudi Arabia Snooker Masters") final against Neil Robertson, making him the first ever professional snooker player to do so.[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O'Sullivan#cite_note-279)
